result.title: Beyond Covers and Titles: Evidence-First Ranking for Robust Cold-Start Recommendation
result.summary: Short-video platforms rank new uploads before anyone has watched them, using content towers that read a video's cover, title and frames. Existing attacks on content-aware recommenders perturb pixels or features and ignore platform re-encoding, and existing defenses train against norm-bounded perturbations that neither match real edits nor preserve recommendation quality. We show with REAP, a realizable attack through {a simulated platform channel (H.264 transcoding, rescaling, cropping and JPEG)}, that packaging edits raise a cold video by 32.0 rank-percentile points in unrelated audiences. We then observe that cold-start ranking does not need the packaging at all: a tower that sees only the video body ranks cold items best. Building on this, we propose Evidence-First Ranking (EFR), which scores cold videos from their body, admits packaging only through a support-gated residual bounded by $γ$, and merges cold and warm rankings by rank percentile, yielding an exact certificate against any packaging edit. On MicroLens-100K, EFR cuts the attack gain by 81% and raises cold-start Recall@100 from 0.1133 to 0.170, while keeping the merged NDCG@10 within 4% of the undefended system.

AI.relevance_reason: 该文研究短视频冷启动推荐中的「包装信息」对抗攻击与防御，核心指标是排序名次与 NDCG，未涉及 latent 推理状态、证据获取或生成式推理；虽有视频内容塔与门控残差，但目标是排序鲁棒性而非推理表示，缺少具体可借鉴线索。
